items.followUp: Define melting point and state two factors that affect it.

rubric.why: Defines boiling point using the condition at which boiling occurs.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a liquid boils when its vapour pressure equals the external (atmospheric) pressure.

rubric.why: Shows the effect of external pressure on boiling point.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that increasing pressure raises the boiling point, or that decreasing pressure lowers it.

accept: non volatile impurities raise boiling point
rubric.why: Identifies the effect of dissolved impurities.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that dissolved non-volatile impurities raise the boiling point.

accept: stronger intermolecular forces higher boiling point
rubric.why: Connects a liquid’s intermolecular attraction to the energy needed for boiling.
rubric.description: Effect of the nature of the liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that stronger intermolecular forces result in a higher boiling point.

modelAnswer: The boiling point is the temperature at which the vapour pressure of a liquid becomes equal to the external (atmospheric) pressure.
Increasing the external pressure raises the boiling point; decreasing it lowers the boiling point.
Dissolved non-volatile impurities generally raise the boiling point.
A liquid with stronger intermolecular forces has a higher boiling point.

items.followUp: What is corrosion? Describe two ways to protect iron from rusting.

accept: iron reacts with oxygen and water
rubric.why: Identifies rust as the product of iron reacting in moist air.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing rusting as the formation of hydrated iron oxide when iron reacts with oxygen and moisture.

rubric.why: Names a protective coating that keeps air and moisture away from the metal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for any of painting, oiling or greasing.

rubric.why: Names protection by coating iron with zinc.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating galvanizing or coating iron with zinc.

rubric.why: Names another protective metallic coating.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for electroplating or naming a suitable protective metal coating such as tin or chromium.

rubric.why: Recognizes that forming a corrosion-resistant alloy can prevent rusting.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that alloying iron, for example to make stainless steel, helps prevent rusting.

modelAnswer: Rusting is the corrosion of iron in the presence of oxygen and moisture, forming hydrated iron oxide.
Metals can be protected from corrosion by painting, oiling or greasing their surfaces.
Iron can be galvanized by coating it with zinc.
It can also be protected by electroplating it with a metal such as tin or chromium.
Alloying iron to make stainless steel also helps prevent rusting.

items.followUp: State four characteristics of a colloidal solution.

rubric.why: Identifies the non-uniform nature of a suspension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.

rubric.why: Describes the relatively large particles in a suspension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that its particles are large enough to be seen, usually with a microscope.

rubric.why: Identifies the settling of suspended particles when left undisturbed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles settle on standing.

rubric.why: Identifies a method for separating suspension particles from the liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the particles can be separated by filtration.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture.
Its particles are relatively large and can be seen, usually with a microscope.
The particles settle down when the suspension is left standing.
The suspended particles can be separated from the liquid by filtration.

items.followUp: Give two differences between a solution and a compound.

rubric.why: Air has variable proportions of its components, unlike a compound with a fixed composition.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that air has variable composition while water has a fixed composition.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a mixture’s physically mixed components from the chemically combined elements in a compound.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that air’s gases are not chemically combined and can be separated physically, whereas hydrogen and oxygen in water are chemically combined.

modelAnswer: Air is a mixture because its gases are present in variable proportions, whereas water is a compound with a fixed composition of hydrogen and oxygen.
The gases in air are not chemically combined and can be separated by physical methods; hydrogen and oxygen in water are chemically combined and water can be decomposed only by chemical methods.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of a sodium ion (Na⁺) in subshells.

rubric.why: Accounts for the extra electron gained by chlorine to form chloride.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Cl⁻ has 18 electrons.

rubric.why: Checks the complete subshell configuration of the 18-electron ion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the full configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶.

modelAnswer: A chlorine atom has 17 electrons; Cl⁻ has gained one electron, so it has 18 electrons.
Electronic configuration of Cl⁻: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶.

items.followUp: State the trend in atomic radius across a period and down a group.

rubric.why: Checks the periodic trend across a row of the periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionization energy generally increases from left to right across a period.

rubric.why: Checks the periodic trend down a column of the periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ionization energy generally decreases down a group.

modelAnswer: Across a period, ionization energy generally increases from left to right.
Down a group, ionization energy generally decreases from top to bottom.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a group and a block in the periodic table.

rubric.why: Identifies the orientation of periods in the periodic table.
rubric.description: A period is a horizontal row.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a period is a horizontal row in the periodic table.

rubric.why: Identifies the orientation of groups in the periodic table.
rubric.description: A group is a vertical column.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a group is a vertical column in the periodic table.

modelAnswer: A period is a horizontal row in the periodic table.
A group is a vertical column in the periodic table.

items.followUp: What are representative elements? Give one example.

rubric.why: Defines transition metals by the characteristic of their d subshells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining transition metals as elements whose atoms or ions have a partially filled d subshell.

rubric.why: Checks that a valid transition-metal example is supplied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as iron (Fe) or copper (Cu).

modelAnswer: Transition metals are elements whose atoms or ions have a partially filled d subshell.
Iron (Fe) is an example of a transition metal.
